title: chore: spec validation added
description:
## Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->

* chore: spec validation added

## Summary

Before publishing a component to the GitLab catalog, the CLI now checks the component's spec file for common mistakes instead of blindly sending it to the server. Specifically, it verifies that the description isn't too long (max 256 characters), that any values listed under `component` are from the allowed set (`name`, `sha`, `version`, `reference`) with no duplicates, and that any ordering defined for inputs only references inputs that actually exist. If an unrecognized key is found in the spec, the tool issues a warning rather than failing outright, since the server has the final say on unknown fields. New tests cover all these validation scenarios.

title: Draft: feat(skills): add testing-df-corporate-proxy harness and skill
description:
## Description

Adds a re-runnable Docker Compose harness and a skill (`.agents/skills/testing-df-corporate-proxy/`) that validates `glab df` behind a corporate upstream proxy — plain, TLS, basic-auth and mutual-TLS proxies, and pre-existing customer CA bundles — for the PyPI, npm and RubyGems families.

**Why.** Corporate networks route all egress through an authenticated/TLS proxy. Manual testing on gitlab-org/gitlab#629431 found that the `df` inspection proxy's upstream hop ignores `HTTPS_PROXY` entirely, plus several related trust/config defects. This makes those requirements reproducible by anyone on the team and gives the fixes a regression net.

**How it works.**

- One Caddy `forward_proxy` service (xcaddy build) bridges an `internal` Docker network to the internet; a runner container per family (`python:3.12-slim`, `node:22`, `ruby:3.3`) sits on the internal network only, so a bypass of the proxy fails hard rather than relying on log heuristics.
- `run.sh` cross-builds `./cmd/glab` from the current checkout for the container architecture and bind-mounts it — no image rebuild on code changes.
- Identity is extracted from the host's `glab auth` (keyring or plaintext, OAuth or PAT) and passed to containers as runtime environment only; nothing under `harness/` ever holds a token.
- Each cell reports the package-manager verdict, a separate `glab api /user` probe classified as `ok|x509|407|cert-required|pem|…` (this is what tells the TLS/auth/mTLS layers apart while the registry hop is blocked), and the CONNECT hosts Caddy saw.
- `matrix/*.tsv` is a **requirements list** (`expected` = `pass` | `fail` for fail-closed negative controls | `blocked` for policy verdicts). `run.sh matrix <family>` prints `MET`/`NOT MET` per requirement and exits non-zero if any is unmet. It does not track "known gaps": red cells are open defects, tracked in gitlab-org/gitlab#629431.

**Current state on this base** (all runs from a fresh clone):

| Family | Requirements | Met | Not met (open defects) |
|---|---|---|---|
| python (pip, uv, poetry) | 17 | 8 | proxied installs, PM-var CA trust, PKCS12/DER client certs, poetry `PIP_CERT` merge |
| node (npm, pnpm, yarn) | 8 | 5 | proxied install, npm `cafile` (env / `.npmrc`) |
| ruby (gem, bundle) | 8 | 6 | proxied install, project-local `.bundle/config` |

Every fail-closed negative control (no CA → `x509`, no creds → `407`, no client cert → `cert-required`) and every CA-merge requirement is met.

**Scope.** Only files under `.agents/skills/testing-df-corporate-proxy/` — no Go changes. Out of scope, listed in the skill: rgdk-provisioned GitLab, TLS-intercepting (MITM) proxy scenario, maven/gradle truststore, go/nuget/cargo runners, macOS-only behavior (Go ignoring `SSL_CERT_FILE` on darwin, LibreSSL system Ruby).

**Reviewer notes.**

- Harness knobs are prefixed `DFH_` because glab resolves any config key from `$UPPERCASE_KEY` in the environment (`CLIENT_CERT=pem` was read as glab's client cert path).
- The entrypoint unsets `BUNDLE_APP_CONFIG`: the official `ruby` image relocates Bundler's project-local config, which hides the `.bundle/config` requirement.
- The pre-push hook's `vale`/`markdownlint` jobs were excluded for this push (`LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE=vale,markdownlint`): on a new branch they lint all files changed vs `origin/main`, which surfaces 52 pre-existing errors in files this MR does not touch (`enabling-https-gdk-in-a-box/SKILL.md`, generated `docs/source/dependency-firewall/package.md`). The MR's own Markdown passes both linters; build, go-lint, go-test, check-generated and lychee ran and passed.

## Related Issues

Related to gitlab-org/gitlab#629431 (glab CLI additional testing and validation). Does not resolve it: the harness establishes the requirements; the defects it reports are fixed separately.

## How has this been tested?

- Manually derived every requirement first (host run against gitlab.com with Caddy as the corporate proxy), then reproduced each in the harness.
- Fresh clone under `$HOME`, macOS arm64, colima, standalone `docker-compose` v5: `./run.sh matrix python|node|ruby` → 17/8/8 requirements, met/not-met exactly as tabled above; `./run.sh cell s2-auth pip --trust cacert -- …` → `api=ok`, `via proxy: gitlab.com:443`; `./run.sh down` leaves no containers; nothing token-shaped on disk (`grep` of `harness/`, `docker inspect` of images).
- Negative paths: not logged in, `DF_PROJECT` unset, unknown scenario/pm/knob/family, checkout on a path Docker cannot bind-mount, Caddy failing to start — each exits early with a one-line actionable error.
- `shellcheck` on all scripts; `markdownlint-cli2` and `vale --minAlertLevel error` on `SKILL.md`; `go test ./internal/commands/skills/...`.
- Not exercised from this machine: amd64 hosts and the `docker compose` plugin form (both are coded for); cold first-run image build time (images were cached; the skill's "5–10 minutes" is an estimate).

title: feat(mr): list and discard pending review comments
description:
## Description

Adds `--draft` to `glab mr note list` and `glab mr note delete` so a pending review can be inspected and individual comments discarded from the CLI. Until now the only way to see or drop a pending comment was the browser.

- `glab mr note list --draft` lists your pending review comments on the MR. Output shows the draft ID, `file:line` when the comment is on the diff, a `(reply to …)` marker for replies, and the body. `--file` still narrows the result; `--type` and `--state` are rejected since drafts have neither. `-F json` returns the raw draft objects.
- `glab mr note delete --draft <id>` discards one pending comment. It fetches the draft first so the confirmation prompt shows the body, and keeps the existing `--yes` rules and destructive annotation.
- `mr note create --draft` and `mr note publish` help now point at the two new flags.
- General drafts come back from the API with an empty `position` object rather than none, so `hasFilePosition` checks for a file path instead of a nil pointer before printing `file:line`.

Follows the plan in #8563.

## Related Issues

Resolves #8563

## How has this been tested?

- `make lint` and `go test ./internal/commands/mr/...` pass.
- New unit tests cover list with drafts, with `--file`, with `-F json`, empty list, API error, and `--draft` combined with `--type`/`--state`; delete with `--yes`, non-interactive without `--yes`, unknown ID, API error, and declining the prompt.
- Manually against a test MR on `gitlab.com`:

```shell
  glab mr note create 1 --draft -m "first"
  glab mr note create 1 --draft --file main.go --line 3 -m "second"
  glab mr note list 1 --draft
  glab mr note list 1 --draft --file main.go
  glab mr note delete 1 --draft <id>
  glab mr note list 1 --draft
```

- `make gen-docs` regenerated `docs/source/mr/note/{create,delete,list,publish}.md`.
